engine.summary: Statistical analysis of tabular data: column profiles, correlation, clustering (k-means, DBSCAN, hierarchical), PCA, anomaly detection (isolation forest, LOF, univariate outlier rules), distribution analysis with normality tests and fits, OLS regression, feature importance, multicollinearity diagnostics and univariate time-series period and anomaly scoring.

surfaces.name: u-insight
surfaces.error_shape: Err(InsightError), whose variant names the reason and holds the values behind it.

surfaces.name: @iyulab/u-insight
surfaces.note: Native JS values in and out, typed in the .d.ts; column-major inputs are objects keyed by column name. Bundler and Node targets; no bundler-less browser build.
surfaces.error_shape: A thrown Error whose code property is the code, with the fields (parameter, index, min, max, got, expected, ...) as its other properties.

surfaces.name: UInsight
surfaces.note: C ABI wrapper over C structs (the cbindgen header), versioned with the crate.
surfaces.error_shape: An InsightException whose ErrorCode is the code, Parameter and Index the fields of those names, and Details the rest.

errors.shape: A refusal carries a stable snake_case 'code' and the fields listed for that code; how it arrives depends on the surface (error_shape).

source.catalog: code_catalog in src/wasm.rs, built from the Code table the refusals are made from; published as codes() in WebAssembly, over the C ABI and as Codes on .NET. What each code means is tabled in README.md, which a test holds equal to the catalog.

operations.summary: A profile of each column of a column-major dataset whose columns may mix numbers, strings, booleans and nulls: its data type (numeric, boolean, categorical or text) and the statistics of that type -- for a numeric column count, missing values, extremes, mean, median, spread and shape; a statistic the data does not define is absent.

checks.claim: The mean, standard deviation, variance, extremes, quantiles (linear interpolation), adjusted skewness and adjusted excess kurtosis of a numeric column equal NumPy's and SciPy's (bias=False), and the same column in a unit 1e-9 or 1e6 times different gives the same shape statistics and scaled location statistics.
checks.reference: NumPy 2.4.6 mean, std(ddof=1), percentile; SciPy 1.17.1 skew and kurtosis with bias=False
checks.method: profiles the 60-value gamma draw of the distribution tests, also scaled
checks.tolerance: 1e-12 (relative) moments and quantiles; 1e-9 skewness and kurtosis

limits: The numeric profile only; boolean, categorical and text profiles, the diagnostic flags and the missing-value handling are covered by unit tests.

operations.summary: The Pearson, Spearman or Kendall correlation matrix of numeric columns, and, with their p-values, the pairs whose correlation is above 0.7 in absolute value; every column needs at least 3 values.

checks.claim: The Pearson, Spearman and Kendall (tau-b) coefficients equal SciPy's, and the pair p-values equal SciPy's default (Kendall's: the exact distribution at these 30 values without ties, SciPy method='auto').
checks.reference: SciPy 1.17.1 pearsonr, spearmanr, kendalltau
checks.method: compares all six pairs of four columns for each method on a seeded NumPy draw, 30 rows by 4 correlated columns (and a target), rounded to six places

limits: The Kendall p-value is exact for n <= 33 without ties (and at any n when at most one pair is on the minority side) and the normal approximation otherwise; the u-analytics tests compare both paths, and the tied-data variance, with SciPy kendalltau. This check compares one tie-free sample of 30 values.

operations.summary: k-means clustering of row-major points with k-means++ initialisation and restarts from a fixed seed: labels numbered by first appearance, centroids, within-cluster sum of squares, iterations and cluster sizes.

checks.claim: On well-separated blobs the partition and the within-cluster sum of squares equal scikit-learn's best of ten restarts.
checks.reference: scikit-learn 1.9.1 KMeans(3, n_init=10)
checks.method: clusters a seeded NumPy draw of three Gaussian blobs of 20 points in 3 dimensions plus two far points, rounded to six places

limits: Only where the optimum is unique and easy to find; k-means is a local search, so overlapping clusters can end in different local optima.

operations.summary: Silhouette scores of a given clustering: the mean over points with a defined silhouette and each point's own (0 for a point alone in its cluster).

checks.claim: The mean silhouette and each point's silhouette equal scikit-learn's for the same labels.
checks.reference: scikit-learn 1.9.1 silhouette_score and silhouette_samples
checks.method: scores the k-means labels of a seeded NumPy draw of three Gaussian blobs of 20 points in 3 dimensions plus two far points, rounded to six places

limits: Euclidean distance; one data set, no singleton clusters.

operations.summary: Principal component analysis of row-major data, optionally on standardized columns: eigenvalues, explained variance ratios, loadings and the scores of each row.

checks.claim: The eigenvalues, explained-variance ratios, loadings (up to sign) and scores (up to sign) equal scikit-learn's PCA; with auto_scale the eigenvalues equal the eigenvalues of the correlation matrix.
checks.reference: scikit-learn 1.9.1 PCA; NumPy 2.4.6 linalg.eigvalsh(corrcoef)
checks.method: fits three components of a seeded NumPy draw of three Gaussian blobs of 20 points in 3 dimensions plus two far points, rounded to six places
checks.tolerance: 1e-9 (relative) eigenvalues and ratios; 1e-6 loadings and scores

limits: Full-rank data; component signs are compared by magnitude.

operations.summary: DBSCAN density clustering of row-major points for a radius epsilon and min_samples: labels (noise apart), cluster count and sizes, noise count and core points.

checks.claim: The cluster labels (numbered by first appearance), the noise points and the core points equal scikit-learn's DBSCAN.
checks.reference: scikit-learn 1.9.1 DBSCAN(eps=1.4, min_samples=4)
checks.method: clusters a seeded NumPy draw of three Gaussian blobs of 20 points in 3 dimensions plus two far points, rounded to six places (4 labels including 8 noise points)

limits: A border point reachable from two clusters is assigned to the first by index order, as scikit-learn does; one data set.

operations.summary: Agglomerative clustering of row-major points by single, complete, average or Ward linkage, cut at a cluster count or a distance threshold: the merge sequence and the labels.

checks.claim: The merge heights of Ward, single, complete and average linkage equal SciPy's, and the cut into three clusters is the same partition.
checks.reference: SciPy 1.17.1 cluster.hierarchy.linkage and fcluster(maxclust)
checks.method: links a seeded NumPy draw of three Gaussian blobs of 20 points in 3 dimensions plus two far points, rounded to six places

limits: Euclidean distance; centroid and median linkage are not offered; distance-threshold cuts are not compared.

operations.summary: Isolation forest anomaly scores of row-major points, and the anomalies above the threshold an expected contamination sets; seeded, 42 when no seed is given.

checks.claim: Planted far points get the highest scores and are the ones flagged, the scores lie strictly between 0 and 1, a seed reproduces the scores exactly, and the same data in a unit 1e-9 or 1e6 times different gives the same flags and scores.
checks.reference: Liu, Ting & Zhou (2008), Isolation Forest, ICDM -- the score 2^(-E[h]/c(n)) lies in (0, 1) and ranks isolated points highest
checks.method: scores a 123-point cloud with three planted points at several scales

limits: The forest is randomised with this crate's generator, so its scores are not compared with scikit-learn's IsolationForest.

operations.summary: Local outlier factor scores of row-major points for k neighbours, and the anomalies above a score threshold or an expected contamination.

checks.claim: The local outlier factor of every point equals scikit-learn's LocalOutlierFactor.
checks.reference: scikit-learn 1.9.1 LocalOutlierFactor(n_neighbors=8)
checks.method: scores a seeded NumPy draw of three Gaussian blobs of 20 points in 3 dimensions plus two far points, rounded to six places

limits: One data set without duplicate points; the anomaly flags (threshold, contamination) are not compared.

operations.summary: The distribution of a numeric sample: ECDF, histogram (by Sturges, Scott, Freedman-Diaconis or a fixed bin count), normal Q-Q points, normality tests (Kolmogorov-Smirnov, Jarque-Bera, Shapiro-Wilk, Anderson-Darling, each omitted with a reason when the sample is outside its range) and optionally fitted distributions.

checks.claim: The Shapiro-Wilk, Jarque-Bera, Kolmogorov-Smirnov and Anderson-Darling statistics and p-values equal SciPy's (Anderson-Darling is reported as the small-sample adjusted A*^2 with the D'Agostino-Stephens p-value).
checks.reference: SciPy 1.17.1 shapiro, jarque_bera, kstest, anderson
checks.method: tests a seeded gamma draw of 57 values with three planted extremes (n = 60), rounded to six places
checks.tolerance: 1e-9 (relative) statistics; 1e-3 to 1e-7 p-values; KS p within 1 %

checks.claim: The maximum-likelihood fits of the normal, exponential and log-normal distributions equal SciPy's, and the Weibull and gamma fits reach SciPy's parameters and a log-likelihood at least as high.
checks.reference: SciPy 1.17.1 norm, expon, lognorm, weibull_min, gamma .fit with the location fixed at 0
checks.method: fits a seeded gamma draw of 57 values with three planted extremes (n = 60), rounded to six places

limits: The Kolmogorov-Smirnov p-value is a finite-sample corrected Kolmogorov approximation (within 1 % of SciPy's exact value at n = 60) and treats the sample mean and standard deviation as known, as SciPy does; a Lilliefors table is not used.
ECDF, histogram and Q-Q plot values, the AIC/BIC ranking and the Grubbs test are covered by unit tests, not compared with a library.

operations.summary: Ordinary least squares regression of a target on named predictor columns: coefficients with p-values, R^2 and adjusted R^2, the F test p-value, VIF of each predictor, fitted values and residuals.

checks.claim: The coefficients, their p-values, R^2, adjusted R^2, the F p-value, the fitted values, the residuals and the VIF of each predictor equal statsmodels' OLS.
checks.reference: statsmodels 0.15.0 OLS with a constant, variance_inflation_factor
checks.method: regresses the target on four predictors of a seeded NumPy draw, 30 rows by 4 correlated columns (and a target), rounded to six places
checks.tolerance: 1e-9 (relative) on estimates and fitted values; 1e-7 on p-values

limits: One data set; heteroscedasticity-robust errors and weights are not offered. In another unit the predictors give the same fit (the intercept and R^2 unchanged, slopes scaled), checked in u-analytics.

operations.summary: The importance of named feature columns for a target by permutation (regression target, seeded), ANOVA F test or mutual information (class target).

checks.claim: The ANOVA F statistic and p-value of each feature equal SciPy's f_oneway and select the informative features; the mutual information equals the plug-in estimate on equal-frequency (Sturges) bins; the permutation importance ranks the features that generate the target above the others, whatever the unit of the target.
checks.reference: SciPy 1.17.1 f_oneway; plug-in mutual information restated in NumPy 2.4.6 from its definition (scikit-learn's mutual_info_classif is a different, nearest-neighbour estimator)
checks.method: scores four features (two informative, one weak, one noise) of a 45-row, three-class draw

limits: Mutual information is the binned estimate, so its values differ from scikit-learn's; permutation importance is randomised and is checked for structure, not values.

operations.summary: The variance inflation factor of each numeric column, and the columns above a threshold (default 10).

checks.claim: The variance inflation factor of each column equals statsmodels' variance_inflation_factor, and equals the same data in a unit a billion times smaller or a million times larger.
checks.reference: statsmodels 0.15.0 variance_inflation_factor on the design with a constant
checks.method: four correlated columns of a seeded NumPy draw, 30 rows by 4 correlated columns (and a target), rounded to six places, and the same columns multiplied by 1e-9, 1e-6 and 1e6

limits: One data set; exact collinearity (infinity) is covered by unit tests.

operations.summary: The 2-norm condition number of the sample covariance matrix of numeric columns (above 30 indicates multicollinearity, Belsley 1991); Infinity for a numerically singular matrix.

checks.claim: The condition number of the sample covariance matrix equals NumPy's cond(cov), and the same data in another unit report the same number (not infinity).
checks.reference: NumPy 2.4.6 linalg.cond(cov(X.T))
checks.method: four correlated columns of a seeded NumPy draw, 30 rows by 4 correlated columns (and a target), rounded to six places, also multiplied by 1e-9, 1e-6 and 1e6

limits: Uniform scaling only: columns in different units change the covariance's conditioning, as they should.

operations.summary: Outliers of a numeric sample by the IQR (Tukey) fences, z-score, modified z-score or Hampel rule: the indices, scores, count, share and the fences used.

checks.claim: The IQR fences (linear-interpolated quartiles, k = 1.5), the z-score fences (sample standard deviation, 3) and the modified z-score centre and MAD match the published definitions, with the same points flagged; the same data multiplied by 1e-9, 1e-6 and 1e6 gives fences scaled by the factor and the same flags.
checks.reference: Tukey (1977) fences; Iglewicz & Hoaglin (1993) modified z-score; NumPy 2.4.6 percentile and median
checks.method: detects outliers in a seeded gamma draw of 57 values with three planted extremes (n = 60), rounded to six places

checks.claim: Grubbs' statistic and critical value (t quantile at alpha/(2n)) equal the closed form, in any unit.
checks.reference: Grubbs (1969); NIST e-Handbook 1.3.5.17; SciPy 1.17.1 t.ppf
checks.method: tests the same data at alpha 0.05, also scaled by 1e-9, 1e-6 and 1e6

limits: Constant or near-constant data (spread below 1e-15 in absolute terms) give no fences; the Hampel identifier is covered by unit tests.

operations.summary: The dominant period of a univariate series by AutoPeriod (Vlachos, Yu & Castelli 2005): periodogram peaks above a permutation threshold confirmed on the autocorrelation function; null when no period passes both stages.

checks.claim: The estimated period of a trended sine of period 7, 12 or 24 is that period; the periodogram and the dominant period are compared with NumPy in the engine that computes them.
checks.reference: series generated from a known period; NumPy 2.4.6 periodogram checked in u-analytics (`seasonality::numpy_reference`)
checks.method: estimates the period of three generated 120-point series

limits: This checks that the operation reaches the verified engine, not the engine's numbers; series with several periods and noise-only series are covered in u-analytics.

operations.summary: An anomaly score for every point of a series by spectral residual saliency (Ren et al. 2019), with the expected value and band at each point and the points judged anomalous.

checks.claim: A spike planted in a noisy sine is flagged (and not more than two other points); the saliency map and the scores equal the published method restated in NumPy in the engine that computes them.
checks.reference: Ren et al. (2019), Time-Series Anomaly Detection Service at Microsoft, KDD; NumPy 2.4.6 restatement checked in u-analytics (`detection::spectral_residual::numpy_reference`)
checks.method: analyses a 96-point series with a spike at index 60

limits: This checks that the operation reaches the verified engine, not the engine's numbers.

operations.summary: Sample autocorrelation of a series for lags 0 to max_lag (biased estimator), with the 95 % white-noise threshold and Bartlett's 95 % limits per lag.

checks.claim: The autocorrelations, the white-noise threshold and Bartlett's limits the operation returns equal the reference's.
checks.reference: statsmodels 0.15.0, statsmodels.tsa.stattools.acf(x, nlags=8, fft=False, alpha=0.05) (limits = confint upper - acf); the same values u-analytics checks its acf against
checks.method: compares lags 0 to 8 of one series of 24 through the request layer both transports share

limits: Checked against the reference above for one series; the default max_lag and the refusals are covered by unit tests, not compared with the reference.

operations.summary: Sample partial autocorrelation of a series for lags 1 to max_lag (below n / 2), by Durbin-Levinson on the biased autocorrelation, with the 95 % threshold.

checks.claim: The partial autocorrelations the operation returns equal the reference's Levinson-Durbin (biased) estimate.
checks.reference: statsmodels 0.15.0, statsmodels.tsa.stattools.pacf(x, nlags=8, method='ldb'); the same values u-analytics checks its pacf against
checks.method: compares lags 1 to 8 of one series of 24 through the request layer both transports share

limits: Checked against the reference above for one series; statsmodels' default method (ywadjusted, denominators n - k) gives different values and is not this estimate.

operations.summary: The augmented Dickey-Fuller unit-root test of a series (no constant, constant, or constant and trend): the statistic, the lags and observations used, and critical values with the verdict at 1 %, 5 % and 10 %.

checks.claim: The ADF statistic, lag count and observations used match the reference implementation, for each model and for a fixed lag count.
checks.reference: statsmodels 0.15 tsa.stattools.adfuller; the same values u-analytics checks its adf_test against
checks.method: tests one generated AR(1) series of 120 under five model and lag settings through the request layer both transports share

limits: Checked against the reference above for one series; the critical values come from MacKinnon's (2010) response surfaces in u-analytics and are not compared here.

operations.summary: The KPSS stationarity test of a series (around a level or a trend): the statistic, the truncation lag, the p-value interpolated in the table of critical values (or the table bound it lies beyond), and critical values with the verdict at 1 %, 2.5 %, 5 % and 10 %.

checks.claim: The KPSS statistic, truncation lag and p-value match the reference implementation for both models and each lag choice (Hobijn, Schwert, fixed).
checks.reference: statsmodels 0.15 tsa.stattools.kpss; the same values u-analytics checks its kpss_test against
checks.method: tests a 60-point AR(1) and a 60-point random walk under six model and lag settings through the request layer both transports share

limits: Checked against the reference above for two series; the critical values are Kwiatkowski et al.'s (1992) Table 1 and the p-value is clamped to [0.01, 0.10].

operations.summary: Seasonal-trend decomposition by Loess (STL) of a series with a known period: trend, seasonal and remainder components, the robustness weights of the outer loop, the strengths of trend and seasonality, and the smoother spans used.

checks.claim: The components, weights, strengths and spans are those of the u-analytics decomposition the request layer calls, which matches statsmodels' STL; every option reaches it unchanged.
checks.reference: u-analytics decomposition::Stl, itself checked against statsmodels 0.15.0 tsa.seasonal.STL on six series (1e-10 relative)
checks.method: decomposes a 48-point seasonal series with default options and with every option set, through the request layer both transports share

limits: The numerical reference is the engine's own check against statsmodels; this crate checks that it hands the request through.

When the remainder is at the data's rounding level (for example two full cycles, which the seasonal smoother interpolates) the robustness weights stay 1; statsmodels marks that rounding noise as outliers, so the weights differ from statsmodels' there.
